reasons.C: Closest period essayist movement: short declaratives mixed with balanced clauses, 'We may smile... but we should not dismiss it' echoing the passage's measured 'We may see... It is better to treat it seriously', with mild first-person hedging and a plain, earnest stance.
reasons.B: Right era and diction with semicolons and an urbane first-person aside, but its ironic epigrams ('they had not heard of the hospitals') are sharper and wittier than the passage's grave, earnest tone.
reasons.A: Modern explanatory prose with contemporary phrasing ('It matters who', 'cohort', 'looks at that peace with fresh and critical eyes') and even, workmanlike rhythm; little of the passage's rhetorical question or period register.
